Quality Management (QM) provides standards and guidelines to confirm the creation of quality work products. As indicated earlier in this document, engagement management incorporates both project management and quality management. However, it is important to distinguish between EY Service Quality (e.g., quality assurance procedures at the engagement management level), and “quality assurance” at the project management level.

  • The firm’s quality assurance procedures at the engagement management level focus on the totality of creating a Superior Client Experience and the engagement processes required to deliver that experience. Delivering technically sound and complete work products are an important part of delivering on our Service Quality promise.
  • Quality assurance at the project management level is focused on applying planned, systematic quality activities so that the project employs all processes needed to meet project requirements.
    The key elements of project QM align to EY’s Service Quality principles, and help our practitioners deliver a superior client experience.

Elements of a Superior Client Experience

Project and activity/work package Leads are responsible for QM, including confirming that their appropriate methodology (e.g., SDA) is implemented correctly.

The key for managing quality is to apply the methods effectively across projects. Project Quality Management is a rigorous process that consists of three core components:
a) Quality planning
b) Quality assurance
c) Quality control

a) Quality planning – must be “planned in, not inspected in”. The cost of non-conformance (rework, failed projects, defects, etc.) is much higher than cost of conformance (training, studies, survey, etc.).
b) Quality assurance – involves continuously improving management processes and the processes that produce work products based on measures is a preventive measure to quality management. This approach injects quality into work products by improving processes, thus avoiding the occurrence of problems as opposed to identifying and removing them at the time of formal/informal review. QA benefits are realized when project teams conduct quality reviews, and analyze data to gauge the variance to standards

Some of the key components of Quality Assurance process are:

  • Extensive review of work products and final work products
  • Enforcement of formal standards and procedures, as defined by EY’s QA program
  • Consistent application of project management processes and techniques
  • Continuous improvement through training and skills transfer
  • Provision of appropriately skilled people

In general, the project management QA process is targeted to projects where there is considerable risk or that are experiencing execution problems. The QA process is designed to help the PM address areas of concern and to confirm quality work is being performed.

Note: Any PM can request a QA for his/her project.

c) Quality control – includes a series of formal/informal reviews to assess predetermined work product standards; these reviews are one way of removing problems from an work product.

This process requires the development of the appropriate acceptance criteria (standard) and the identification of appropriate individuals to review an work product and agree to final approval.

Some of the items considered during quality control prevention phase are:

  • Have quality criteria been defined for each work product (this would be documented on the Quality Form during project structuring /planning)?
  • Have the training, coaching and knowledge transfer prepared team members for their work?
  • Are the estimates of effort and planned duration sufficient to produce acceptable quality work?
  • Have standards and procedures been developed and are they being followed?

Some of the items considered during quality control inspection phase are:

  • Is sufficient time allotted for the assessment of work products against agreed quality criteria?
  • Are team reviews working effectively?
  • Are both program and project quality reviewers involved in the assessment and approval of work products?
  • Are approvals of work products going smoothly?
  • Have there been any change requests regarding defects in approved work products?
